title: Benchmarking LLM Inference on Desktop-Scale NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Clusters
abstract: arXiv:2611.20289v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Two NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 systems connect directly over 200 GbE to serve larger language models and increase inference capacity, but the benefits depend on how they are deployed. We benchmark 17 open-weight checkpoints spanning dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, 8B to 235B parameters and four weight precisions on one and two RDMA-connected systems. Using vLLM, we compare tensor parallelism (TP=2), pipeline parallelism (PP=2) and a two-replica baseline at concurrency 1 to 64, with three independent launches per configuration. TP=2 delivers a median 1.59x peak-throughput gain over one Spark, versus 1.39x for PP=2 and has higher throughput in 93 of 96 matched comparisons with separated 95% Welch intervals. It reduces unloaded inter-token latency to 0.52x to 0.73x of one Spark, whereas PP=2 provides little reduction. TP=2 also achieves the highest goodput under a strict 100 ms inter-token latency objective wherever both strategies

translated_title: 在桌面级 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell 集群上对大语言模型推理进行基准测试
translated_abstract: 两台 NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 系统通过 200 GbE 直接互连，可以服务更大的语言模型并提升推理能力，但其收益取决于部署方式。我们在单台和两台 RDMA 互连的系统上，对 17 个开放权重检查点进行基准测试，涵盖稠密架构与混合专家（MoE）架构、8B 至 235B 参数规模以及四种权重精度。使用 vLLM，我们在并发度 1 至 64 的条件下比较张量并行（TP=2）、流水线并行（PP=2）和双副本基线，每种配置独立启动三次。TP=2 相比单台 Spark 带来中位数 1.59 倍的峰值吞吐量提升，而 PP=2 仅为 1.39 倍，且在 96 组匹配比较中有 93 组（95% Welch 置信区间相互分离）显示 TP=2 吞吐量更高。TP=2 将无负载词间延迟降低至单台 Spark 的 0.52 至 0.73 倍，而 PP=2 几乎没有降低。在严格的 100 毫秒词间延迟目标下，只要两种策略均可满足要求，TP=2 都能实现最高的有效吞吐量（goodput）。
tldr: 该研究对两台 RDMA 互连的桌面级 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell（DGX Spark GB10）集群上的大模型推理进行了系统基准测试，发现张量并行（TP=2）在吞吐量和延迟上均优于流水线并行和双副本部署，峰值吞吐量中位提升达 1.59 倍并将词间延迟降至单机的一半以下。
en_tdlr: This study benchmarks LLM inference on two RDMA-connected desktop-scale NVIDIA Grace Blackwell (DGX Spark GB10) systems and shows that tensor parallelism (TP=2) outperforms pipeline parallelism and two-replica deployment, delivering a median 1.59x peak-throughput gain and reducing inter-token latency to roughly half of a single system.
